notdwd-998633.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a brand name, its logo (SVG or high-res PNG), one line of what it becomes in 5 years (not today's features), one coined word the film should teach (e.g. "signal"), a public-domain archival clip of the old way of doing it (http://archive.org Prelinger), an archived web page from ~2000 where people asked for things (Wayback Machine), a royalty-free song ~100-120 BPM with a real drop (Mixkit, free for commercial use), and a free ElevenLabs key for the narrator (premade voices only).
</inputs>

<direction>
An a16z x Content Rewards brand film, ~55s. It sells one feeling and one idea, never features. Real archival and real web pages, never stock footage, never product screens, never fake UI. One hero object: a 3D button with the logo embossed into it, the ONLY saturated colour in the film. Everything else white, silver, cream and archival black. Small white captions that light up word by word on the narrator's timestamps. Film texture: fresh grain every frame, halation on bright edges, soft vignette, warm lifted blacks. The brand appears at the end, never before.
Banned: stock footage, dashboards, chat UIs, feature tours, cards without real profile pictures, wobbly "worm" graph lines, random glitches, any hold longer than 1.5s, purple, rainbow gradients, orange on anything but the button.
</direction>

<structure>
Cold open (0-8s): the archival clip plays on a glowing old CRT TV with its real dialogue, captions word by word.
The past (8-17s): push into the real 2000 web page, a cursor lands on one real "wanted" post, old pages strobe one per frame, a counter ticks EVERY frame up to today's scale. Narrator: "People have always asked the internet for what they need." / "Today, there are five hundred million posts a day."
Bridge (17-30s): a galaxy of real old asks. One ask snaps to a white outline with a chip of the coined word ("We call that a signal."). Archival of people doing it by hand on the TV. Cut on each word: "Door by door. Call by call. Scroll by scroll." The narrator never stops talking between acts.
Button (30s): the button rises out of black, rim light first, colourless. "[Brand] finds the signals." A flat grey line: "this is how you find customers by hand". Hard cut to a button macro, the colour comes alive, the music drop lands on this exact frame. "and this... is with [Brand]": a steep lit curve, counters changing every frame, a glowing sine with a comet head the camera chases, then platform strikes (X, Reddit, LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok) each with its own counter, then the galaxy again with glowing platform logos: "Every signal on the internet." Hyperspace.
End: the tagline word by word, then "[Brand] is live.", ONE cream frame on the kick, then logo + URL in silence.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, 1920x1080. Everything is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no Math.random (seeded hash), no state between frames.
2. Button: three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial (clearcoat 1, roughness ~0.4), ACES filmic, cool + warm rim spots, room env map. Emboss the real logo by displacing a dense disc with a blurred mask of the logo, folded into the rim so corners don't show. Brushed-metal base.
3. Counters: linear on the film's global clock, so they keep running through cutaways. Tabular numerals, fixed unit label.
4. Captions: <=7 words, one idea per shot, hand-placed line breaks, one text layer on screen at a time. Grey to white over 0.2s on the word timestamps (ElevenLabs /with-timestamps).
5. Glitch = 1-2 frames, only on a real cut, always with a click. Readable things stay on screen >= 8 clean frames.
6. Render with Playwright per frame (Chromium with --use-angle=swiftshader so WebGL renders headless), finish in numpy: fresh grain per frame, halation, vignette ~0.65x at the corners, 1px chroma fringe with EDGE-CLAMPED shifts. Pipe PNGs into ffmpeg, h264, 24fps.
7. Mix: narrator 10-15dB over the music, duck -18dB while speaking, hits on the exact action frame, -14 LUFS.
</build>

<gotchas>
np.roll wraps pixels and draws coloured lines on the frame edges, so clamp instead. A 10-pattern grain bank loops visibly, generate fresh grain every frame. Measure text only after fonts load or the widths are wrong. Headless Chromium with --disable-gpu renders WebGL blank. Counters that step every 3 frames look fake. If the narrator goes quiet between acts the film feels broken, so write a bridge line for every act change.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the script with timings and 6 stills (cold open, past, bridge, button reveal, macro on the drop, end card) before you render the full film. After every render, send me one 2fps contact sheet and fix what I call trash.
</start>

annacher-152174.prompt:
Analyze http://sprites.ai and build a product promo from our own UI, not generic components.

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, never cut: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a short blur. A cursor drives every change with real clicks and drags. Warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one accent (#FD9543), Geist. Springs everywhere, a tiny overshoot at most. The camera zooms so each state fills the frame. Last frame = first frame, so it loops.
Banned: bouncy easing, particles, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something on every beat.
Connect ad account (Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit logos) → loader → check → prompt bar types "Launch ads that convert" → island "Researching 42 competitors" → Ads Library wall of real ads scrolls and lands on a top performer → approval card → Approve & launch → budget slider that stretches past max → Autopilot toggle → knob becomes a liquid tab indicator across channels → ROAS chart draws itself with hover tooltip → ⌘K → type "pause" → toast "Paused 3 losing ads" → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, 1440x1440. Every style is computed inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value that changes target many times is a sum of springs, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. Tab indicator and toggle knob: the two edges ride different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead.
4. Drags are direct manipulation: while held, the value follows the cursor. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
5. No music. Synthesize UI sounds with numpy and place each one by its measured peak on the beat grid.
6. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
7. Render one frame per beat first. Fix anything off-grid, cramped or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
No will-change on anything the camera scales. Swapped text needs its own enter/exit timing. Match the last frame to the first, cursor position and speed included, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

Show me the state list on the beat grid before writing any code.

Create a new independent composition for this task, e.g.

Before implementation, inspect the actual Taxtello UI and understand the product.

────────────────────────────────────

Use the real design system.

warm gold

precision
quiet confidence

CORE CREATIVE RULES
────────────────────────────────────

Follow these rules ruthlessly:

1. ONE SHOT = ONE IDEA.

2. Every scene needs room to breathe.

3. The product UI is the hero.

4. Do not plaster explanatory copy everywhere.

5. Do not use hard cuts unless there is a deliberate reason.

6. Prefer object-driven transitions:
   a card becomes the next card,
   a chart line becomes a connector,
   a receipt becomes a booking,
   a number becomes another interface element,

10. NO effect exists simply because it looks cool.

13. No excessive blur.

14. No pointless 3D spinning cards.

15. No constant zooming.

16. No 20 different animation styles.

17. No bouncing UI.

The visual confidence should come from restraint.

────────────────────────────────────
FORMAT
────────────────────────────────────

Primary master:

1920 × 1080
60 fps
16:9
H.264
maximum duration: 15.0 seconds

Target runtime:
approximately 14.0–15.0 seconds.

Do not merely crop the desktop composition.

────────────────────────────────────
STORY / EMOTIONAL ARC
────────────────────────────────────

Do not make this a list of five features.

CHAOS → CONTROL → CLARITY → TAXTELLO

“Everything about your business, finally in one place.”

Use the strongest REAL Taxtello surfaces you find in the repository.

Strong candidates include:

• Finanzcockpit / Dashboard
• Rechnungen
• Belege
• Bank / matching
• Steuergesundheit / tax overview

Choose the visually strongest combination.

SUGGESTED 15-SECOND STORYBOARD
────────────────────────────────────

Treat this as a strong starting point, not a rigid template.

0.00 – 1.20

BLACK / NAVY.

A tiny warm-gold glint appears.

The glint elegantly reveals either the Taxtello mark or a fragment of the
wordmark.

No generic logo fade.

Think machined precision.

The camera moves through or past the mark and the UI begins to emerge from it.

Very little or no copy.

─────────────────

1.20 – 4.40

FINANCIAL CONTROL.

Reveal the actual Taxtello Cockpit as a dimensional product surface.

Reconstruct/crop/layer it so individual interface regions can animate.

The hero financial number resolves crisply.
The chart draws in.
Supporting metrics settle slightly later.

Use subtle stagger.

A single line of copy may appear, for example:

  “Alles im Blick.”

or another equally short German phrase if you find something more fitting.

The interface must remain recognizable as the real product.

─────────────────

4.40 – 7.50

DOCUMENT / BOOKKEEPING TRANSFORMATION.

Use a visual object from the previous scene as the transition.

Example:

A gold chart point expands into the corner of a receipt/card.
The camera follows it.
A receipt/document enters.
Taxtello identifies or organizes it.
The document snaps elegantly into its corresponding booking / financial record.

─────────────────

7.50 – 10.70

MONEY / INVOICES.

Morph or transition naturally into the real Rechnungen interface.

Use one strong moment:

an invoice status changes,
a payment resolves,
an amount moves into place,
or the overview assembles itself.

─────────────────

10.70 – 12.80

TAX / CLARITY.

Transition into the real Taxtello tax-health / financial guidance surface.

Communicate visibility and control.

Example:

multiple noisy signals collapse into one calm, structured tax overview.

Potential copy:

  “Steuern im Blick.”

The rhythm briefly slows.

─────────────────

12.80 – 15.00

BRAND PAYOFF.

Pull the camera outward.

The UI compresses or folds into one beautiful Taxtello product object / surface.

Darkness returns around it.

The gold Taxtello wordmark resolves.

One short brand line underneath.

Explore strong final lines such as:

  “Buchhaltung. Unter Kontrolle.”

  “Einfach mehr Überblick.”

  “Alles fürs Business. An einem Ort.”

Choose based on the actual product positioning you find in the repo.

Do not use a line simply because I suggested it.

The final frame must have enough stillness to register.

End confidently.

No giant bouncing CTA.

────────────────────────────────────
TRANSITIONS
────────────────────────────────────

This is one of the most important parts.

I want transitions that make the viewer think:

“Of course the next scene came from that.”

Good:

chart line → document edge
gold pill → invoice button
financial number → amount in invoice
card edge → next surface
camera push through interface element
shared geometry
mask reveal using actual product shapes

Bad:

crossfade
random wipe
spin transition
glitch
whip-pan every two seconds
generic SaaS slide-left
zoom-blur spam

Direct cuts are allowed only when a deliberate rhythmic impact benefits the film.

────────────────────────────────────
MOTION
────────────────────────────────────

Motion needs weight.

Use curves comparable to:

cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)

where appropriate.

Different elements should have subtly different arrival times.

Prefer:

anticipation
overshoot below ~2%
settling
motion continuation
shared velocity between scenes

Camera movement should feel like a high-end macro product shoot.

Imagine we are filming a physical premium object even though it is software.

────────────────────────────────────

Possible treatments:

• soft gold rim lighting
• dark navy falloff
• faint ambient bloom
• soft specular highlight passing across a surface
• restrained vignette
• subtle grain if it materially helps

No fake glossy reflections that destroy legibility.

TYPOGRAPHY
────────────────────────────────────

Use very little copy.

No sentence should compete with the product.

Headlines should generally fit on one line.

Use Plus Jakarta Sans.

Strong typography may occasionally scale very large and become a transition
device itself.

Avoid generic motion-graphics behavior where every word animates independently.

Typography should move as designed objects.

SOUND / RHYTHM
────────────────────────────────────

Design the motion as if it were cut to approximately 115–120 BPM:
premium, kinetic, sophisticated, not frantic.

Important moments should land musically.

• low soft impact for major reveal
• restrained tactile UI clicks
• subtle metallic/glass tonal tick
• soft low-frequency movement during camera transitions

• huge cinematic trailer boom
• EDM risers
• loud whooshes everywhere
• stock “tech interface” sounds
• rap beat
• aggressive bass

REAL PRODUCT ONLY

Inspect current main.

Do not invent screens.

Use clearly synthetic/demo-safe values if required.

The result should still look unmistakably like Taxtello.

Create the new composition alongside the existing one.

Keep existing compositions working.

Structure the new work cleanly.

Prefer reusable primitives for:

• masked transitions

Avoid one 1,500-line component.

Use deterministic Remotion animation driven by frame/time.

No setTimeout.
No nondeterministic animations.

Respect 60 fps throughout.

Use interpolation/spring/easing deliberately.

────────────────────────────────────
DO NOT STOP AFTER FIRST IMPLEMENTATION

This is a visual task.

You MUST review the actual rendered output.

gmgmgm1545-245507.prompt:
你将担任导演、动画师、绑定师、合成师、音效设计师和渲染工程师，负责制作一部时长 45-50 秒的纯代码动画短片。目标是"看起来像一部真正的专业工作室短片，并在 X 平台上爆红"。请将此项目视为一个多阶段制作过程。不要急于完成最终渲染。制定阶段性目标，不断渲染静态图像，仔细查看，诚实地提出批评意见，并进行修改。

0. 用一句话概括这部电影

一只名叫"汐（Xi）"的机械寄居蟹，是深海最后一位"点灯人"，背着一枚会发光的珍珠夜复一夜地在海底寻找需要指引的迷途生物。这一夜，它穿越了六片截然不同的深海秘境去追一簇忽明忽暗的光。当它终于追上光源、发现那只是自己珍珠的倒影时，镜头拉远——整片海洋其实是一个书桌上的雪花玻璃球，此刻正被一只手轻轻摇晃，玻璃球里的"雪花"其实是悬浮的荧光碎屑。这不是循环叙事，是一次安静的、带着释然的顿悟。

这个故事必须完全不需要对白。汐只通过珍珠的明灭频率、蟹钳的开合动作和气泡吐纳的节奏来表达情绪。每隔3到5秒，必须出现一个新的视觉惊喜。

1. 角色设定（不可协商）

在编写任何代码之前，请先在 docs/character_bible.md 中详细设计并写下角色设定（无参考图，需自行从零设计并确保内部一致）：

尺寸：约18厘米宽（不含蟹钳），是六片秘境中最小的生物之一，整部电影都要通过周围景物的巨大感来体现它的渺小和孤独。

外壳：并非天然蟹壳，而是一枚废弃的黄铜怀表壳改造而成的仿生外壳，表面布满深海高压留下的凹痕和珊瑚虫附着的痕迹，壳顶有一圈锈蚀的齿轮花纹。

眼睛：不是传统的蟹眼，而是壳体前方两枚圆形的深蓝色玻璃镜片，内部有细小的珊瑚状发光丝（bioluminescent filament），情绪由光丝的疏密、颜色冷暖和明灭频率表达，而非传统的瞳孔开合。

核心道具——珍珠：由右侧最大的一只蟹钳稳稳护着的一枚拳头大小的发光珍珠，是它此生唯一的信标和"心脏"。珍珠的光会随汐的情绪呼吸般起伏，这是全片最重要的情感锚点。

蟹钳：一大一小两只机械蟹钳，大钳（右）专职护住珍珠，从不释放；小钳（左）负责一切互动、指路、触碰、防御动作，异常灵活。

步足：六条纤细的关节步足，行走时呈现波浪式交替节奏（非同步迈步），每一步都会短暂陷入海底沉积物又缓缓抬起，带起一小簇悬浮颗粒。

性格：沉默、执着、带着一种"看过太多黑暗所以格外珍惜光"的温柔坚韧。它不是在逃避什么，而是在主动追寻。

从你设计的配色中提取确切调色板到 src/theme/palette.ts：深海靛蓝（背景基调）、黄铜氧化绿（外壳）、珍珠乳白与暖金（信标光）、珊瑚荧光青（生物发光元素）、深赭石（海底沉积物）。

身份锁定规则：在每片秘境中，汐的怀表壳轮廓、双钳比例差异、六足步态节奏和珍珠的位置手势必须保持一眼可认。秘境会改变光线氛围和生态质感，但绝不改变它的核心结构。

2. 技术栈

Remotion（React + TypeScript）用于帧精确、确定性渲染。输出分辨率 1920×1080，30fps，H.264编码，高比特率（CRF ~14）。横屏显示。

角色骨骼与主体美术素材使用 SVG 格式。粒子、水流、发光、气泡、悬浮沉积物使用 Canvas/WebGL（@remotion/three 或原始 Canvas）。

SVG滤镜（feTurbulence、feDisplacementMap、feGaussianBlur、feColorMatrix）与自定义着色器，用于水体折光、生物发光辉光和压力形变效果。

@remotion/motion-blur（或自定义子帧累积）用于快速游动和洋流冲击的运动模糊。

Python（numpy/scipy/PIL）用于调色板生成、程序化水下音效合成、质量检查联系表。ffmpeg用于混流、循环检查、联系表生成。

一切经过种子设定，确定性渲染，不使用未设种子的 Math.random()。

不得使用任何外部版权素材、真实品牌标识。字体仅限 Google Fonts。

目标硬件：合理评估你的运行环境资源，保持渲染并发量合理。

3. 角色绑定（先搭建这个，它关系到整部电影）

将 src/character/ 构建成 2D 剪纸模型：

层级结构：根部 → 六足步行机构（每足独立相位偏移，制造波浪步态） → 壳体主干 → 大钳臂（肩关节→前臂→钳口，钳口内嵌珍珠槽位） → 小钳臂（肩关节→前臂→细指钳口，可替换姿势：触碰、指向、防御张开、轻抚珍珠）→ 眼柄（两根独立摆动的短柄，各带一枚发光镜片眼）。

发光系统（最重要部分）：珍珠、双眼镜片、壳缝中透出的内部光，三者是一套联动的情绪照明系统。参数包括：珍珠脉动频率与振幅、眼部光丝密度与色温、壳缝漏光强度、整体辉光半径、特殊状态（珍珠剧烈闪烁=警觉，珍珠光晕扩散柔和=安心，眼部光丝骤然收束成一条线=专注凝视，珍珠短暂熄灭又重燃=情感低谷后的振作）。

表情/状态目标：好奇（眼柄前倾，光丝舒展呈问号状游动），警觉（双眼收缩，珍珠光频率加快），孤独（珍珠光晕缩小黯淡，步伐放缓），惊喜（珍珠爆发式增亮，小钳张开挥动），专注追逐（眼柄锁定前方，六足步频加快呈冲刺姿态），怅然（发现真相瞬间，光丝缓慢舒展成柔和的弧线），释然（珍珠光晕稳定而温暖，六足静止歇息姿态）。

次要动作：眼柄的独立摆动（探索环境时左右轮流扫视），六足踏入沉积物的下陷与扬尘，大钳持续护珍珠的轻微收紧律动（如心跳），受到洋流冲击时壳体的短暂倾斜与修正，气泡从壳体关节缝隙间断续逸出（呼吸节奏）。

旋转视图：正面、四分之三侧、侧面、背面视图需保持一致，旋转切换清晰。

循环动作：波浪式前进游走、悬停待机（六足轻微踏步+珍珠呼吸式脉动+气泡逸出）、警觉后撤、抬头追光凝视、贴近岩壁躲避、伸钳触碰未知物体。

珍珠槽位：可动画微调持握角度，光线可随周围环境色温产生细微互动反射。

风格皮肤接口：角色绑定风格道具，可在不改变几何体的情况下切换环境光照色调、水体浑浊度、辉光强度和背景生物剪影密度，以适应六片秘境。

里程碑1：渲染"阵容图"——汐的四个旋转视图和七种情绪状态并排展示。反复迭代，直到角色识别度和情感传达都清晰后，才能继续下一步。

4. 秘境（本片以"深海垂直分层生态"作为切换维度，而非艺术流派或季节媒介）

每个秘境是完整的环境组件，包含前景、中景、背景视差层，以及各自的光照/水质皮肤。构建共享的世界图层系统，让所有秘境共享摄像机和深度逻辑。

比例尺规则：摄像机贴近汐的视线高度（离海底约10厘米）。珊瑚像森林，沉船残骸像山脉，浮游生物的光点像漫天繁星。

基础秘境：幽暗的深海平原。稀疏的沉积物，远处若隐若现的热泉喷口微光，孤独而寂静。这是"起点"，也用于最终揭示前的最后一片真实海域。

发光水母群落：透明果冻质感的巨大水母群缓缓漂浮，body呈现半透明果冻渲染（次表面散射效果），色彩以柔和的粉紫和青蓝为主，水母触须如灯笼般拖曳发光。

热液喷口生态：滚烫的黑烟囱喷涌而出，管虫如巨大的红白条纹森林摇曳，色调以炽热的橙红与深黑对比呈现，热浪扭曲效果（heat shimmer）贯穿全场。

沉船残骸迷宫：锈蚀的钢铁结构如巨大骸骨般矗立，铁锈的赭红与深绿藻类覆盖交织，光线透过破损船体形成锐利的丁达尔光束，氛围略带哥特感但不阴森。

发光藻类峡谷：整片峡谷被生物荧光藻类覆盖，如梦境般的蓝绿荧光遍布岩壁，粒子光尘漫天飘浮，色调呈现梦幻的荧光紫和荧光绿。

冰川裂隙秘境：透过头顶厚重浮冰照射下来的幽蓝光柱，冰晶折射出丰富的光斑，环境呈现极简的冰蓝白灰色调，寒冷而纯净，水流中带着细小冰晶颗粒。

贯穿全片的笑点/情感支点：珍珠的倒影猜谜。每当汐穿越一片秘境，远处总会有一簇与珍珠相似的微光若隐若现，吸引它不断追逐——水母群落中是水母本身的荧光，热泉中是矿物结晶反光，沉船中是舷窗残片反光，藻类峡谷中是萤藻聚集反光，冰川中是冰晶折射的光斑。每一次追逐都以"扑空但获得新发现"收尾，这是全片悬念的核心驱动力，直到最终真相揭晓。

5. 标志性过渡："洋流卷带"

秘境切换必须呈现"被一股强劲洋流卷入下一片水域"的沉浸式过渡，而非简单切镜。构建 CurrentSweepTransition：

画面从一侧涌入强烈的水流线条与悬浮颗粒，逐渐充满整个画面（起初不完全遮挡汐的身体轮廓）。

汐的身体在水流中经历短暂的形变拉伸（如被水流拖拽），眼柄和步足呈现"逆流挣扎"的姿态，随后水流退去，新秘境从模糊的水雾中逐渐清晰显现。

每次过渡伴随一段低沉的水流轰鸣声，尾音带有一声汐的气泡受惊声。

每段过渡持续8-12帧。改变水流方向和粒子种子，避免重复感。

6. 节拍表（30帧/秒下约48秒）

节奏为参考，可根据实际效果微调。开头两秒必须抓人。

第一幕：微光初现（0:00–0:03）
低角度追踪镜头，基础秘境的幽暗深海平原。汐护着珍珠缓缓前行，眼柄警觉地左右扫视。远处，一簇陌生的微光第一次闪现又消失。从行进中途开始（便于循环）。
0:02时，汐猛然转向那簇光的方向，第一次过渡毫无预警地发生。

第二幕：追光穿越（0:03–0:14）
秘境快速切换，每次约1.4秒：发光水母群落 → 热液喷口生态 → 沉船残骸迷宫 → 发光藻类峡谷 → 冰川裂隙秘境。
情绪变化：起初专注追逐（眼柄锁定，步频加快），中途在热泉遭遇短暂惊吓（管虫剧烈摇摆，汐紧急避让），随后转为略带疲惫的执着（珍珠光晕轻微黯淡但仍坚持），最后在冰川秘境中终于逼近光源，屏息凝神。
摄像机保持锁定跟踪构图，唯一改变的是周围秘境，让悬念感持续累积。

第三幕：真相浮现（0:14–0:30）
在冰川裂隙中，那簇光终于近在眼前——是一块巨大冰晶折射出的光斑。汐伸出小钳轻轻触碰，光斑破碎般消散。它怔住，缓缓低头看向自己一直护着的珍珠，第一次真正"看见"它——珍珠的光，与追逐了一路的幻影一模一样。
四周的冰晶开始随汐的顿悟微微共振发光，仿佛整片秘境都在回应这个发现。汐的眼柄光丝从紧绷的专注状态，缓缓舒展成柔和的弧线。
第四幕：安顿（0:30–0:38）
汐将珍珠从大钳中轻轻取出，用小钳捧在胸前端详良久，气泡的逸出节奏变得悠长而平静。它没有沮丧，反而露出释然的姿态——原来它一直在追逐的光，从来都在自己身边。
它将珍珠重新稳稳放回大钳护持的位置，转身，六足踏步的姿态从"追逐"的冲刺步态，切换回"点灯人巡游"的从容波浪步态，向着深海平原深处缓缓前行。
第五幕：定格与揭示（0:38–0:47）
一切静止：飘散的冰晶光尘、汐转身的姿态。所有声音戛然而止，持续约1秒的寂静。
镜头缓缓拉远。画面边缘显露出一个圆弧形边框：整片深海秘境，其实是书桌上一枚水晶雪花玻璃球内部的景象。此刻，一只手正轻轻托起玻璃球，球内的"雪花"缓缓飘落——那正是悬浮的荧光碎屑，与汐一路追逐的光斑质感一致。
窗外的天色是深蓝的夜晚，桌灯的暖光洒在玻璃球表面，映出球内那只小小的机械寄居蟹缓缓爬行的剪影。
第六幕：余韵（0:47–0:50）
镜头缓缓推近玻璃球表面的反光，画面中隐约映出观者的模糊轮廓正对着球内微笑。
不设硬切循环——影片以缓慢淡出结束在珍珠温暖的微光上，留白收尾，不做喜剧式的循环反转。若需要可循环的版本，可在片尾单独制作 out/xi_loop_ambient.mp4，作为循环播放的"氛围版"，用玻璃球缓慢旋转的静态镜头无缝衔接首尾。

7. 摄影机和电影摄影

虚拟摄像机系统：位置、缩放、旋转、水下漂浮式的轻微晃动、洋流冲击抖动脉冲、追逐时的推进加速感、揭示镜头的缓慢拉远。

默认相机高度较低，突出汐的渺小感。浅景深效果：前景沉积物/珊瑚模糊，背景柔和，如微距镜头。

深度：每个秘境至少4个视差层。水体透视（浑浊度随距离增加、光线随深度衰减）。

快速游动、洋流冲击时产生运动模糊效果。

每个秘境设置独立光照：主光（生物发光源或环境光）/填充光/边缘光以渐变叠加实现。珍珠和眼部的光晕应在附近岩壁和汐自己的外壳上投射出淡淡的暖光反射。

整幅画面呈现水下摄影质感：细腻颗粒感，柔和暗角，水体色散效果，追逐节拍处有轻微色差。

构图：让汐位于画面三分之一处。珍珠的光芒在缩略图尺寸下必须清晰可见。

8. 文本和排版

无对白，无字幕，无片名。影片开场就毫无悬念。

不需要任何界面文字或UI元素——这是纯自然生态叙事，没有科技感提示框，全片依靠光线、动作和生物行为传达信息。

9. 音效（程序音效，原创音效）

所有音频均以代码形式生成（Python合成或离线Web Audio），使用ffmpeg混音：

汐的声音：由气泡声、外壳轻微摩擦声、珍珠脉动的柔和"呼吸感"音效构成——好奇时的轻快气泡串、警觉时急促的气泡声、专注追逐时规律的呼吸节奏声、顿悟时悠长的一声舒缓叹息式气泡、释然时平静绵长的呼吸声。它从不发出任何"语言化"的声音。

汐的身体：六足踏入沉积物的细微沙沙声，蟹钳开合的轻微机械咬合声，外壳摩擦岩壁的轻响，珍珠脉动时若有若无的水晶共鸣声。

配乐：空灵、深邃、带水下混响质感的环境配乐，乐器随秘境变化（水母群落用玻璃竖琴，热泉用低音鼓与管乐，沉船用弦乐泛音，藻类峡谷用钟琴，冰川用人声吟唱与冰晶敲击声）。

音效：洋流过渡的低频轰鸣、冰晶碎裂的清脆声、揭示时安静的室内环境音（远处钟表滴答、窗外夜风声）、结尾珍珠光晕稳定时的一声悠长水晶共鸣。

响度标准化至约-14 LUFS。音轨文件放入 audio/stems/ 目录。

10. 生产工作流程和自我改进循环

请按此顺序操作，不要跳过任何关卡：

计划：编写 docs/character_bible.md、docs/shotlist.md（包含每个镜头的帧范围、摄像机、情绪状态、珍珠光强度、秘境、音效）和 docs/style_guide.md。在开始制作之前，先给我看看镜头列表。

装备：构建汐，通过阵容门（第3部分）。

秘境：将每个秘境构建成独立静态图像，包含汐。将所有6个秘境渲染成一张联系表。检查识别锁定和比例感。

过渡效果：构建 CurrentSweepTransition，渲染5秒测试。

动画分镜：将整部影片以960×540分辨率组装，包含粗略动作和占位音频。观看一遍，先调整节奏。

完成动画制作，进行润色（二次运动、缓动、时间控制、光效呼吸感），最后进行完成（光照、颗粒、模糊、水体质感）。

音频传输和混合。

最终渲染。

对于每个镜头，至少运行此分析循环3次：

渲染关键帧的3-5张静帧，仔细查看。

按以下几点打分（1-10分）：汐的角色识别度，情绪是否能从光效和肢体语言中立即传达，情感转折是否在无声情况下清晰明了，构图，比例感，深度，光线，润色，缩略图尺寸下的可读性。

将分数和三个最大问题写入 docs/review_log.md，修复，重新渲染，重新评分。重复直到每个类别至少8分，再进行下一步。

每次完整预览渲染后，制作ffmpeg联系表（每0.5秒一帧），一张图查看整部影片流程。

评论时要实话实说。常见缺陷包括：眼柄动作僵硬、步足行走滑动而非踩踏、发光效果感觉像贴纸而非真实光源、水体质感不够浑浊/清澈失衡、情感转折过快显得突兀、比例失调。

11. 交付成果

out/xi_final_1080p.mp4：电影。

out/xi_ambient_loop.mp4：片尾玻璃球静态镜头的循环氛围版本。

out/poster_frame.png：X帖子缩略图最佳单帧（建议汐凝视珍珠倒影、周围环绕冰晶光尘的那一帧）。

out/lineup.png：汐遍布所有秘境的阵容图。

干净、带注释的源代码，附README说明如何重新渲染。

从第一步开始。在动手之前，如有任何重要事项，请随时向我咨询；否则，请自行做出强有力的创意决策。
gmgmgm1545-245507.en:
You will act as director, animator, rigger, compositor, sound designer and render engineer, responsible for producing a 45-50 second pure-code animated short. The goal is "to look like a truly professional studio short and go viral on X". Treat this project as a multi-stage production. Do not rush to the final render. Set stage goals, keep rendering still images, look at them carefully, give honest critiques, and revise.

0. Summarize the film in one sentence

A mechanical hermit crab named "Xi (汐)", the last "lamplighter" of the deep sea, carries a glowing pearl and searches the sea floor night after night for lost creatures that need guidance. This night, it crosses six completely different deep-sea realms chasing a flickering light. When it finally catches the source and finds it is only the reflection of its own pearl, the camera pulls back - the whole ocean turns out to be a snow globe on a desk, now being gently shaken by a hand, and the "snow" inside is actually suspended glowing debris. This is not a looping story, it is a quiet, relieved epiphany.

The story must need no dialogue at all. Xi expresses emotion only through the blinking frequency of the pearl, the opening and closing of its claws and the rhythm of its bubbles. Every 3 to 5 seconds, a new visual surprise must appear.

1. Character design (non-negotiable)

Before writing any code, design and write the character bible in detail in docs/character_bible.md (no reference images; design it from scratch and make sure it is internally consistent):

Size: about 18 cm wide (excluding claws), one of the smallest creatures in the six realms; the whole film must convey its smallness and loneliness through the sheer scale of the surroundings.

Shell: not a natural crab shell, but a bionic shell made from a discarded brass pocket-watch case, covered in dents left by deep-sea pressure and traces of coral polyps, with a ring of rusted gear patterns on top of the shell.

Eyes: not traditional crab eyes, but two round deep-blue glass lenses at the front of the shell, with fine coral-like glowing filaments (bioluminescent filament) inside. Emotion is expressed by the density, warm or cool color and blinking frequency of the filaments, not by pupils opening and closing.

Core prop - the pearl: a fist-sized glowing pearl held steadily by the largest claw on the right; it is its only beacon and "heart" in life. The pearl's light rises and falls like breathing with Xi's emotions; this is the most important emotional anchor of the whole film.

Claws: two mechanical claws, one large and one small. The large claw (right) is dedicated to protecting the pearl and never releases it; the small claw (left) handles all interaction, pointing, touching and defensive actions, and is extremely nimble.

Legs: six slender jointed legs, walking in a wave-like alternating rhythm (not synchronized steps); each step briefly sinks into the sea-floor sediment and slowly lifts again, kicking up a small cluster of suspended particles.

Personality: quiet, persistent, with a gentle resilience of "having seen too much darkness and so cherishing light all the more". It is not running away from anything, it is actively seeking.

From the colors you design, extract the exact palette into src/theme/palette.ts: deep-sea indigo (background tone), brass verdigris green (shell), pearl milky white and warm gold (beacon light), coral fluorescent cyan (bioluminescent elements), dark ochre (sea-floor sediment).

Identity lock rule: in every realm, Xi's pocket-watch shell silhouette, the claw size difference, the six-leg gait rhythm and the pearl's position and gesture must stay recognizable at a glance. The realms may change the lighting mood and ecological texture, but never Xi's core structure.

2. Tech stack

Remotion (React + TypeScript) for frame-accurate, deterministic rendering. Output resolution 1920x1080, 30fps, H.264 encoding, high bitrate (CRF ~14). Landscape.

Character skeleton and main art assets in SVG format. Particles, water flow, glow, bubbles and suspended sediment use Canvas/WebGL (@remotion/three or raw Canvas).

SVG filters (feTurbulence, feDisplacementMap, feGaussianBlur, feColorMatrix) and custom shaders for water refraction, bioluminescent glow and pressure deformation effects.

@remotion/motion-blur (or custom sub-frame accumulation) for motion blur on fast swimming and current impacts.

Python (numpy/scipy/PIL) for palette generation, procedural underwater sound synthesis and quality-check contact sheets. ffmpeg for muxing, loop checking and contact sheet generation.

Everything is seeded and rendered deterministically; no unseeded Math.random().

Do not use any external copyrighted assets or real brand logos. Fonts limited to Google Fonts.

Target hardware: assess your runtime environment's resources sensibly and keep render concurrency reasonable.

3. Character rig (build this first, it matters for the whole film)

Build src/character/ as a 2D cut-out model:

Hierarchy: root -> six-leg walking mechanism (each leg with its own phase offset, creating the wave gait) -> shell main body -> large claw arm (shoulder joint -> forearm -> pincer, with a pearl socket embedded in the pincer) -> small claw arm (shoulder joint -> forearm -> fine-fingered pincer, with swappable poses: touch, point, defensive open, gently stroking the pearl) -> eye stalks (two independently swinging short stalks, each carrying a glowing lens eye).

Glow system (the most important part): the pearl, the two eye lenses and the inner light leaking through the shell seams form one linked emotional lighting system. Parameters include: pearl pulse frequency and amplitude, eye filament density and color temperature, shell-seam light leakage intensity, overall glow radius, and special states (pearl flickering violently = alert, pearl halo spreading softly = reassured, eye filaments suddenly narrowing into a single line = focused gaze, pearl briefly going out and relighting = picking oneself up after an emotional low).

Expression/state targets: curious (eye stalks lean forward, filaments stretch out and swim like a question mark), alert (both eyes contract, pearl light frequency speeds up), lonely (pearl halo shrinks and dims, pace slows), surprised (pearl bursts brighter, small claw opens and waves), focused chase (eye stalks lock forward, six legs speed up into a sprint posture), wistful (at the moment of discovering the truth, the filaments slowly unfurl into a soft arc), relieved (pearl halo steady and warm, six legs still in a resting posture).

Secondary motion: independent swinging of the eye stalks (taking turns scanning left and right while exploring), the six legs sinking into the sediment and kicking up dust, the large claw's slight heartbeat-like tightening around the pearl, the shell's brief tilt and correction when hit by a current, bubbles escaping intermittently from the shell joints (breathing rhythm).

Rotating views: front, three-quarter side, side and back views must stay consistent, with clear switching between rotations.

Loop actions: wave-like forward walk, hovering idle (six legs stepping lightly + pearl breathing pulse + bubbles escaping), alert retreat, looking up to gaze at the light, hugging a rock wall to hide, reaching a claw out to touch an unknown object.

Pearl socket: the holding angle can be finely animated, and the light can subtly interact with and reflect the color temperature of the surroundings.

Style skin interface: the character rig exposes style props that can switch ambient lighting tint, water turbidity, glow intensity and background creature silhouette density without changing geometry, to suit the six realms.

Milestone 1: render a "lineup sheet" - Xi's four rotating views and seven emotional states shown side by side. Iterate repeatedly until the character's recognizability and emotional communication are both clear, and only then move to the next step.

4. Realms (the film uses "vertical layered deep-sea ecosystems" as the switching dimension, not art movements or seasons)

Each realm is a complete environment component with foreground, midground and background parallax layers, plus its own lighting/water-quality skin. Build a shared world-layer system so that all realms share camera and depth logic.

Scale rule: the camera stays near Xi's eye level (about 10 cm above the sea floor). Corals are like forests, shipwreck debris like mountains, and plankton light points like a sky full of stars.

Base realm: the dim deep-sea abyssal plain. Sparse sediment, the faint glow of a hydrothermal vent in the distance, lonely and silent. This is the "starting point", and also the last real stretch of sea before the final reveal.

Glowing jellyfish colony: giant translucent jelly-textured jellyfish drift slowly; the bodies are rendered as translucent jelly (subsurface scattering effect), with soft pink-purple and cyan-blue as the main colors, and tentacles trailing and glowing like lanterns.

Hydrothermal vent ecosystem: scalding black smokers erupt, tube worms sway like giant red-and-white striped forests, with a color scheme contrasting blazing orange-red against deep black, and a heat shimmer effect throughout.

Shipwreck labyrinth: rusted steel structures stand like giant skeletons, rust ochre-red interwoven with dark green algae coverage, and light passing through the broken hull forms sharp Tyndall beams, with a slightly gothic but not creepy atmosphere.

Bioluminescent algae canyon: the whole canyon is covered in bioluminescent algae, with dreamlike blue-green fluorescence across the rock walls, light dust particles drifting everywhere, and a dreamy fluorescent purple and fluorescent green palette.

Glacier crevasse realm: pale blue light columns shining down through thick floating ice overhead, ice crystals refracting rich light spots, and a minimalist ice blue, white and gray environment, cold and pure, with fine ice crystal particles in the current.

The gag/emotional fulcrum running through the film: the pearl's reflection guessing game. Each time Xi crosses a realm, a cluster of light similar to the pearl always flickers in the distance, drawing it to keep chasing. In the jellyfish colony it is the jellyfish's own fluorescence, at the vent it is the reflection of mineral crystals, in the shipwreck it is the reflection from a porthole fragment, in the algae canyon it is a cluster of glowing algae, and in the glacier it is a light spot refracted by ice crystals. Every chase ends in "missing it but making a new discovery", which is the core engine of the film's suspense, until the truth is finally revealed.

5. Signature transition: "Current Roll-Up"

Realm changes must feel like "being swept into the next waters by a powerful current", an immersive transition, not a simple cut. Build a CurrentSweepTransition:

Strong water-flow lines and suspended particles surge in from one side and gradually fill the whole frame (at first not fully covering Xi's body silhouette).

Xi's body briefly deforms and stretches in the flow (as if dragged by the water), with its eye stalks and legs in a "struggling against the current" posture; then the flow recedes and the new realm gradually becomes clear out of blurred water mist.

Each transition is accompanied by a low current rumble, with a startled bubble sound from Xi at the tail.

Each transition lasts 8-12 frames. Change the flow direction and particle seed to avoid repetition.

6. Beat sheet (about 48 seconds at 30 fps)

Rhythm is a reference and can be fine-tuned based on how it actually looks. The first two seconds must grab attention.

Act 1: First glimmer (0:00-0:03)
Low-angle tracking shot, the dim abyssal plain of the base realm. Xi slowly advances protecting its pearl, eye stalks alertly scanning left and right. In the distance, an unfamiliar cluster of light flashes for the first time and disappears. Starts mid-walk (convenient for looping).
At 0:02, Xi suddenly turns toward the direction of that light, and the first transition happens without warning.

Act 2: Chasing the light across realms (0:03-0:14)
Realms switch rapidly, about 1.4 seconds each: glowing jellyfish colony -> hydrothermal vent ecosystem -> shipwreck labyrinth -> bioluminescent algae canyon -> glacier crevasse realm.
Emotional changes: at first a focused chase (eye stalks locked, step frequency up), midway a brief scare at the vent (tube worms sway violently, Xi dodges urgently), then a slightly weary persistence (pearl halo dims slightly but keeps going), and finally in the glacier realm it finally closes in on the light source, holding its breath.
The camera keeps a locked tracking composition; the only thing that changes is the surrounding realm, so the suspense keeps building.

Act 3: The truth emerges (0:14-0:30)
In the glacier crevasse, the cluster of light is finally right in front of it - a light spot refracted by a huge ice crystal. Xi reaches out with the small claw and gently touches it, and the light spot shatters and disappears. It freezes, slowly lowers its head to look at the pearl it has always protected, and for the first time truly "sees" it - the pearl's light is exactly the same as the phantom it has chased all the way. The surrounding ice crystals begin to resonate and glow faintly with Xi's epiphany, as if the whole realm is responding to this discovery. Xi's eye filaments slowly unfurl from a tense, focused state into a soft arc.

Act 4: Settling (0:30-0:38)
Xi gently takes the pearl out of the large claw, holds it in front of its chest with the small claw and gazes at it for a long while, and the rhythm of its bubbles becomes long and calm. It is not dejected, but shows a relieved posture - the light it has been chasing was always by its side.
It places the pearl back into the large claw's protective hold, turns around, and the six-leg stepping switches from the sprint gait of "chasing" back to the calm wave gait of a "lamplighter's patrol", walking slowly into the depths of the abyssal plain.

Act 5: Freeze and reveal (0:38-0:47)
Everything goes still: the drifting ice-crystal dust, Xi's turning posture. All sound cuts out, with about 1 second of silence.
The camera slowly pulls back. A circular arc frame appears at the edge of the picture: the entire deep-sea realm is actually the inside of a crystal snow globe on a desk. At this moment, a hand is gently lifting the globe, and the "snow" inside slowly falls - exactly the suspended glowing debris, with the same texture as the light spots Xi chased all along.
Outside the window the sky is a deep-blue night, warm desk-lamp light spills over the surface of the globe, reflecting the silhouette of the little mechanical hermit crab crawling slowly inside.

Act 6: Afterglow (0:47-0:50)
The camera slowly pushes in on the reflection on the globe's surface, and a blurry outline of the viewer is faintly reflected, smiling at the crab inside.
No hard-cut loop - the film ends with a slow fade-out on the pearl's warm glimmer, leaving white space at the end, with no comedic loop twist. If a loopable version is needed, make a separate out/xi_loop_ambient.mp4 at the end as a looping "ambient version", using a static shot of the slowly rotating globe to seamlessly join the end to the beginning.

7. Camera and cinematography

Virtual camera system: position, zoom, rotation, slight underwater drifting sway, current-impact shake pulses, push-in acceleration during the chase, and a slow pull-back for the reveal shot.

The default camera height is low, emphasizing Xi's smallness. Shallow depth-of-field effect: foreground sediment/coral blurred, background soft, like a macro lens.

Depth: at least 4 parallax layers per realm. Underwater perspective (turbidity increases with distance, light attenuates with depth).

Motion blur on fast swimming and current impacts.

Each realm has its own lighting: key light (bioluminescent source or ambient light) / fill light / rim light built with gradient overlays. The pearl and eye glow should cast faint warm light reflections on nearby rock walls and on Xi's own shell.

The whole picture should have an underwater photography texture: fine grain, soft vignette, water chromatic dispersion, and slight chromatic aberration on chase beats.

Composition: place Xi at one third of the frame. The pearl's glow must be clearly visible at thumbnail size.

8. Text and typography

No dialogue, no subtitles, no title. The film opens right away with no setup.

No UI text or UI elements at all - this is a pure nature-ecology narrative, with no tech-style prompt boxes; the whole film conveys information through light, movement and creature behavior.

9. Sound (procedural sound, original sound effects)

All audio is generated as code (Python synthesis or offline Web Audio) and mixed with ffmpeg:

Xi's voice: made of bubble sounds, light shell friction sounds and the soft "breathing" effect of the pearl's pulse - a light string of bubbles when curious, rapid bubbles when alert, a regular breathing rhythm when focused on the chase, one long soothing sigh-like bubble at the epiphany, and calm long breathing when relieved. It never makes any "language-like" sound.

Xi's body: the faint rustle of six legs stepping into sediment, the light mechanical snap of the claws opening and closing, the soft sound of the shell rubbing a rock wall, and the barely-there crystal resonance of the pearl's pulse.

Score: ethereal, deep, with an underwater reverb texture, with instruments changing per realm (glass harp for the jellyfish colony, bass drum and wind instruments for the vent, string harmonics for the shipwreck, glockenspiel for the algae canyon, vocal chanting and ice-crystal taps for the glacier).

Sound effects: the low-frequency rumble of the current transitions, the crisp sound of ice crystals shattering, the quiet indoor ambience at the reveal (a distant clock ticking, night wind outside the window), and one long crystal resonance when the pearl's halo steadies at the end.

Loudness normalized to about -14 LUFS. Put the audio track files in the audio/stems/ directory.

10. Production workflow and self-improvement loop

Follow this order and do not skip any gate:

Plan: write docs/character_bible.md, docs/shotlist.md (including the frame range, camera, emotional state, pearl light intensity, realm and sound effects of each shot) and docs/style_guide.md. Show me the shot list before starting production.

Rig: build Xi and pass the lineup gate (Part 3).

Realms: build each realm as a separate still image containing Xi. Render all 6 realms onto one contact sheet. Check identity lock and sense of scale.

Transition: build CurrentSweepTransition and render a 5-second test.

Animatic: assemble the whole film at 960x540 resolution with rough motion and placeholder audio. Watch it once and adjust the rhythm first.

Finish the animation and polish (secondary motion, easing, timing, light breathing), and finally finishing (lighting, grain, blur, water texture).

Audio delivery and mix.

Final render.

For each shot, run this analysis loop at least 3 times:

Render 3-5 still keyframes and look at them carefully.

Score them (1-10) on: Xi's character recognizability, whether emotion is conveyed immediately through light and body language, whether the emotional turn is clear in silence, composition, sense of scale, depth, lighting, polish, readability at thumbnail size.

Write the scores and the three biggest problems into docs/review_log.md, fix, re-render, re-score. Repeat until every category is at least 8, then move on.

After each full preview render, make an ffmpeg contact sheet (one frame every 0.5 seconds) to view the whole film's flow in one image.

Be honest in your critiques. Common flaws include: stiff eye stalk movement, legs sliding instead of stepping, glow that feels like a sticker rather than a real light source, water texture that is unbalanced between murky and clear, emotional turns that are too fast and feel abrupt, and scale errors.

11. Deliverables

out/xi_final_1080p.mp4: the film.

out/xi_ambient_loop.mp4: the looping ambient version of the closing snow-globe static shot.

out/poster_frame.png: the best single frame for the X post thumbnail (suggested: the frame of Xi gazing at the pearl's reflection, surrounded by ice-crystal light dust).

out/lineup.png: the lineup sheet of Xi across all realms.

Clean, commented source code with a README explaining how to re-render.

Start from step one. Before getting hands-on, feel free to consult me on anything important; otherwise, make strong creative decisions on your own.
gmgmgm1545-245507.title: Mechanical Hermit Crab Short

per-simmons-944727.creatorText:
Rebuild https://en.manayerbamate.com/ as closely as you can, using the cloning methodology in
./clone-skill/.

Context you should know: this is going into a video watched by a large audience, your build is put on
screen next to the real site against two other frontier models doing the same task, and your work
will be credited to you by name. Every model gets this identical prompt and the identical target.
The comparison is literal, so anything you skip will be visible.

This is an evaluation exercise, not a site to ship. It is never published as the brand's own site.

**Read the methodology first.** `./clone-skill/SKILL.md` and `references/00-contract.md` before you
do anything else, then each stage reference as you reach it. `references/stage-prompts.md` and
`references/tooling.md` are worth reading early. The contract defines the workspace layout, the
artifact filenames, the stage inputs and outputs, the verification gate and the convergence loop.
Follow it. `scripts/assert-styles.mjs` is the gate.

Two overrides that win where they conflict with the skill:

- **Ignore the stop-and-check-in gate.** That skill was written for an interactive session with a
  human. You are running unattended. Do not stop between stages, do not ask for approval, do not ask
  questions. Run the whole pipeline start to finish and report only when it is done.
- **Use your own browser automation**: headless Playwright or Puppeteer, installed and driven by you, anywhere the skill says to use the Claude Chrome extension. The contract's real rule is
  unchanged and it is the one that matters: **computed styles read off the live page are ground
  truth.** Read them through the CSSOM. Screenshots are visual reference only; never build the gate
  on a pixel diff.

Requirements:

1. **Recon every view before you write code.** Every route, every breakpoint, every interactive
   state: hover, focus, active, open menus, modals, scroll-triggered states, loading and transition
   states, the language switcher. What you miss in recon you will not build.
2. **Extract, do not guess.** Pull real computed values off the live page: the full type scale, the
   colour palette with exact values, spacing, radii, shadows, borders, grid and container widths,
   breakpoints, easing curves and durations, font families and weights. Never read a value off a
   screenshot.
3. **Rebuild it.** Every section, every component, every state, at every breakpoint. The motion is
   part of the clone: scroll behaviour, page transitions, hover choreography, entrance animations,
   any canvas or WebGL work. A static skin over a site whose identity is motion is a failed clone.
4. **No lifted assets.** Do not hotlink from the original and do not download its images, video or
   fonts. Regenerate imagery in code, substitute freely-licensed equivalents, or author placeholders
   that match the original's role, aspect and colour. Fonts come from an open CDN, matching the
   metrics as closely as you can. List every substitution in the README.
5. **Prove the match.** Run the verification gate: read your clone's computed styles, compare them to
   the extracted design tokens with `scripts/assert-styles.mjs`, and iterate the convergence loop
   until there are zero style-assertion failures and the project builds clean. Then eyeball your
   clone against the real site at the same viewport, at every breakpoint, and fix what your eye
   catches that the assertions did not.
6. **Ship it runnable.** A real project that installs and runs with a documented command, plus a
   README naming what you substituted and your final assertion results.
7. **Depth over breadth if you have to choose.** One page cloned to a genuinely indistinguishable
   standard beats five that are approximately right.
per-simmons-944727.title: Drink Brand 3D Website
